items.title: NICE backs sebetralstat, an oral on-demand treatment for hereditary angioedema attacks
items.summary: NICE final draft guidance recommends sebetralstat as an oral on-demand option for hereditary angioedema attacks in people aged 12 and over on the NHS in England and Wales.

items.title: NHS England pilots a new approach to the Budget Impact Test for innovative medicines
items.summary: ABPI has published a guest blog from NHS England on its pilot of a new approach to the UK Budget Impact Test, to support adoption of innovative medicines.

items.title: Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Medicines Optimisation Committee (IMOC) minutes: new minutes listed: IMOC Minutes 2026 10 (October 2026)
items.summary: The list at this address now includes "IMOC Minutes 2026 10 (October 2026)", which was not in the list stored on 2026-10-16. It has not been read by a person; open it to see what it says.

items.title: DHSC medical technology director discusses Part IX Drug Tariff reform
items.summary: Interview with David Lawson of the Department of Health and Social Care covering reform of Part IX of the Drug Tariff, which governs medical devices and appliances prescribed in the community.

items.title: PAGB Self-Care Census 2026: pharmacy central to the self-care pathway
items.summary: PAGB's 2026 Self-Care Census of 3,058 UK adults found 91% acted within 48 hours of symptoms and 57% used an OTC medicine in that window, more than twice the next most common action (searching online, 23%). PAGB CEO Michelle Riddalls set out what it means for community pharmacy.

items.title: UK modernises gene therapy definition in regulatory revamp
items.summary: The UK government has proposed a mechanism-based legal definition of gene therapy medicinal products, aligned with the EU. It drops the biological-origin requirement so synthetic products and genome-editing treatments fall under the established MHRA framework.

items.title: Progress with NHS England pilots of alternative funding approaches
items.summary: An FOI request on the NHS England pilots to speed adoption of innovative medicines, a commitment under the UK-US pharma trade deal, shows details were still being finalised on 6 November. The pilot is planned to go live from April 2027.

items.title: ViiV wins CHMP backing for paediatric HIV drugs
items.summary: CHMP has issued a positive opinion for ViiV Healthcare's paediatric HIV treatments, supporting expanded treatment access in Europe.

items.title: Hazardous medicines: turning consensus into safer health care
items.summary: British Journal of Nursing, Volume 35, Issue 21, Page S3-S3, November 2026.

items.title: West Yorkshire ICB prescription spend among highest in England
items.summary: An analysis by Cured Pharmacy of NHSBSA data puts NHS West Yorkshire ICB third for prescribing spend at £292.42 per person, with the highest items per person (35.5).

items.title: Tryngolza approved in EU for severe hypertriglyceridaemia
items.summary: The EU has approved Tryngolza, an RNA therapy, for severe hypertriglyceridaemia; it reduces triglycerides and pancreatitis risk.

items.title: SNOMED CT UK Drug Extension: grouper concepts being removed, supplier survey closes 20 November 2026
items.summary: NHS England is removing the five grouper concepts from the SNOMED CT UK Drug Extension in Phase 2 of its alignment to the SNOMED International national drug extension model, scheduled for Quarter 4 2026, and replacing them with Refsets.

items.title: UKHSA concerned over ‘low uptake’ of pharmacy MenB jab offer
items.summary: Less than one in three eligible 18- and 19-year-olds have had a first dose of the free MenB vaccine which is currently being offered in pharmacies. items.title: ICB refuses to fund GPs for transitioning patients from discontinued Levemir
items.summary: One ICB has rejected a proposal from GP leaders seeking funding for practices switching patients from Levemir (insulin detemir) to alternatives.

items.title: NHSE sets out requirements for pharmacy prescribing including GP communication
items.summary: NHS England has set out requirements for pharmacies delivering prescribing services, including sending GP practices information on all prescribing activity.

items.title: Pharmacies can begin providing new NHS prescribing services
items.summary: Approved community pharmacies can start delivering five new prescribing pathways announced under this year's Community Pharmacy contractual framework (Google Alert, The Pharmacist).
